facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a 2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions on the face and neck
The lesions were round, hypopigmented macules and were symmetrically distributed in the affected area
The macules had appeared on his cheeks 2 years earlier and had gradually coalesced
The size of the lesions ranged from approximately 2 to 3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
There was no hair growth at the site of the lesions
He was previously treated for tinea versicolor, without success
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation
Stroma formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor
Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of multiple asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules with subepidermal tumors and elastosis is consistent with Degos disease.
The patient's lesions are characteristic of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis, with multiple, round, hypopigmented macules on the face and neck.
The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords and fibrous connective tissue stroma are consistent with an epidermal nevus.
The patient's presentation of multiple, hypopigmented macules with subepidermal tumors and elastosis could be consistent with an adnexal tumor.

rationales.F02: Hypopigmented macules are more typical of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis and epidermal nevus
rationales.F05: Absence of hair growth is not typical of epidermal nevus
rationales.F06: Previous treatment for tinea versicolor without success rules out this condition
rationales.F07: Plate-like subepidermal tumor with cord-like connections is highly suggestive of epidermal nevus or adnexal tumor
rationales.F08: Clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation are characteristic of certain adnexal tumors and epidermal nevi
rationales.F10: Marked elastosis is more typical of epidermal nevus and adnexal tumor

frontier_selector.rationale: Histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords and marked elastosis support Adnexal tumor, with Epidermal nevus being a close runner-up due to similar histopathologic features but less comprehensive match to the vignette.
